projects.title: koma
projects.summary: A volume-dial symbol grown into a full brand, interface and sound system for a spatial-audio speaker.
projects.overview: Self-initiated concept for koma, a spatial-audio speaker brand. The identity starts from one idea, the volume knob, and carries it through a living design system, a room-calibration web app and the product itself.
projects.challenge: The first sketch of the symbol, a ring of growing dots, read as a loading spinner: the opposite of what a premium audio brand wants to say. It also fell apart at small sizes, where the smallest dots disappeared. The brand needed a mark with a clear meaning that would hold up from a 16 px favicon to a speaker grille.
projects.solution: The ring became a dial: seven dots on a 270° arc that grow clockwise, with the 90° gap at the bottom acting as the knob's stop. The name nods to the musical comma, the smallest tuning interval, and the symbol moves the same way, in small precise steps. An optical version keeps all seven dots legible below 40 px. The same geometry becomes the knobs of the Room Calibrator web app, the perforated grille of the koma one speaker and a seven-note sonic logo. The system is documented live, in Spanish and English: colour, motion and sound tokens, usage rules, a component state matrix and a night mode.

projects.title: PsychoStart
projects.summary: A running-shoe brand built to look fast, from the emblem to the launch-day storefront.
projects.overview: Identity and launch storefront for PsychoStart Running Shoes: a brand designed in 2012 to read as speed at a glance, then brought online in 2025 for the debut of the Velocity 1.0 runner.
projects.challenge: A new running brand has seconds to prove it belongs next to the big names. PsychoStart needed an identity that reads as speed and grit from across a store aisle, and a product page that carries the same energy online without getting in the way of the sale.
projects.solution: A lightning-struck “P” emblem and a bold wordmark set the pace, backed by a forest-and-lime palette and the rallying line “Ignite your run.” The system runs from tongue and insole logos to shoe boxes, a “Built to run, made to win” stamp and retail displays. For the Velocity 1.0 launch, the storefront hero puts the shoe front and centre over a giant wordmark, with an inline colourway switcher (Forest, Lime and Black), a clear price and add-to-cart, and drop alerts that turn a release date into an event.

projects.title: Ledn
projects.summary: Launch animations and kinetic type that make bitcoin finance easy to follow.
projects.overview: Motion design for Ledn, the bitcoin financial services company: product launches, newsletter promos and a fast, meme-literate kinetic-type series that makes crypto jargon easy to follow and hard to scroll past.
projects.challenge: Bitcoin finance is loud, technical and full of jargon. Ledn needed motion that could launch new products with confidence, explain them in seconds and still feel native in fast-moving social feeds, without losing the trust a financial brand depends on.
projects.solution: Two registers, one system. For product moments, from the B2X launch to BTC and USDC trading and the weekly newsletter, clean animations built on Ledn's teal palette and glowing coin icons keep the message calm and credible: instant trades, no fees, earn interest. For social, a high-energy kinetic-type series cuts crypto vocabulary like Multisig, UTXO, HODL and Proof of Reserves into punchy, meme-literate edits that teach while they entertain. The result is a brand that sounds credible on the product page and fluent in the feed.

cover.alt: Frames from the Ledn motion reel: B2X and Ledn logo animations, a trading launch title and kinetic crypto type

projects.title: SimpliCare
projects.summary: A clinic brand that feels calm, clear and trustworthy from the street to the front desk.
projects.overview: Brand identity for SimpliCare Medical Clinics: a calm, confident system that tells patients they're in good hands before they walk through the door.
projects.challenge: Clinics often look either cold or generic. SimpliCare needed to signal medical competence and modern efficiency while feeling warm and approachable to patients who may arrive anxious.
projects.solution: A clean, rounded wordmark puts care at the centre: the “i” in the middle of the name is set in olive to single out the individual patient. Deep navy brings authority, olive and soft neutrals bring warmth, and the type stays legible at every size. The system is built for the real world: a navy storefront with dimensional lettering that reads from across the street, premium business cards and stationery, and branded pens for the front desk, with the same palette and type carried into digital.

projects.title: Expariences
projects.summary: A sun-and-moon identity that makes a holistic practice feel grounded and credible.
projects.overview: Identity for Expariences, a French-language holistic education practice: a sun-and-moon symbol and a warm, earthy palette that make a spiritual practice feel grounded, trustworthy and easy to say yes to.
projects.challenge: Holistic services run on trust. Expariences needed to express its mystical, nature-led philosophy without tipping into cliché, and to look professional enough for clients to commit to a full programme.
projects.solution: A sun cradling a crescent moon captures balance in a single line-drawn mark, paired with a refined serif wordmark. Forest green and gold anchor the palette, with terracotta and ochre accents for warmth. The system extends to the tools of the practice itself: a weekly intentions agenda, client agreements and letterhead, business cards and envelopes, buttons and a branded tee, so every touchpoint feels as considered as the sessions.

projects.title: The Tire Terminal
projects.summary: Roll-ups, a tire-care brochure and social for the GTA's tire superstore.
projects.overview: Event and marketing collateral for The Tire Terminal, the GTA's tire superstore since 2001: one confident red-and-black system that earns the trust of fleet managers and everyday drivers alike.
projects.challenge: Sell to two very different buyers, owner-operators running commercial fleets and drivers shopping for their own car, without splitting the brand in two. And turn dense technical tire knowledge into something customers actually want to read.
projects.solution: A bold red-and-black system anchored by the Tire Terminal mark and a consistent set of line icons. Two roll-up banners split the offer by audience: commercial tires, 24/7 road service and fleet management on one; passenger tires, custom wheels and seasonal storage on the other, both closing with the partner brands as proof of range. “The Roundup”, a tri-fold guide, explains sizing codes, wheel and tire anatomy and routine maintenance in clear illustrated panels the counter team can hand to every customer. Social templates for reviews, seasonal promotions and hiring carry the same voice online, so the showroom, the trade-show booth and the feed all read as one trusted business.

projects.title: Patlon
projects.summary: An aviation identity and website that make a ground-support supplier look world-class.
projects.overview: Brand identity and website for Patlon, a supplier of aviation ground-support equipment: a confident yellow-on-slate system that looks as dependable as the machines it sells.
projects.challenge: In aviation, buyers choose suppliers they trust with safety-critical equipment. Patlon needed a brand that projects precision and reliability to airports worldwide, and a website that turns that trust into quote requests.
projects.solution: A “P” mark with an aircraft cut into its negative space, set in aviation yellow on deep slate, reads instantly at any size, from a pen to a uniform. The responsive website leads with a clear promise, “Ground Support Equipment, Engineered for Aviation”, backs it with proof points (24/7 global support, certified to aviation standards, 20+ years trusted by airports) and gives buyers two direct paths: explore products or request a quote. Stationery and uniforms carry the same system from the office to the apron.

projects.title: Sheridan Seating
projects.summary: A brand built on strength, durability and comfort for telescopic seating and stages.
projects.overview: Brand system for Sheridan Seating Inc., maker of telescopic bleachers and retractable stages: one bold navy-and-orange identity that sells engineering to schools, arenas and theatres.
projects.challenge: Seating is a high-stakes purchase judged on engineering, safety and longevity, but the people who sign off are rarely engineers. Sheridan needed to look as solid as its product and explain complex systems clearly across sales, print and digital.
projects.solution: A sunburst “S”, its rays evoking tiered rows and stage lights, pairs with a heavy, confident wordmark in navy and orange. A custom icon set explains configurations at a glance, and the line “Strength. Durability. Comfort.” gives sales one clear promise. The system runs across stationery, product brochures such as the Applaud™ Bleacher System, technical stage drawings, shipping packaging, a product app and social content, so every touchpoint reinforces the same engineered quality.

projects.title: Caitlyn's Cakes
projects.summary: A sweet mint-and-pink bakery brand that turns every takeout order into a gift.
projects.overview: Brand identity and packaging for Caitlyn's Cakes Bakery: a playful mint-and-pastel system designed so every box, bag and cup that leaves the counter sells the bakery all over again.
projects.challenge: A neighbourhood bakery competes on delight. Caitlyn's needed a look as tempting as its cupcakes, one that stands out on the counter and keeps working on the street, at the office and on social feeds after the sale.
projects.solution: A hand-lettered script wordmark and a cheerful cupcake icon set the tone, in a mint, pink and buttery-yellow palette that feels fresh and indulgent. The packaging does the selling: windowed takeout boxes put the cupcakes on display, while kraft cup sleeves and mint carry bags turn every coffee and order into a small advertisement for the bakery.

projects.title: Maggie Carolina
projects.summary: A warm hand-drawn brand for a knitting and crochet maker, from yarn bands to webshop.
projects.overview: Boutique brand identity for Maggie Carolina Knitting & Crochet: a hand-drawn script and a rich burgundy palette that make handmade pieces feel premium, giftable and worth the price.
projects.challenge: Handmade goods are often undervalued. Maggie Carolina needed a brand that keeps the warmth of craft while looking polished enough to sell online, at markets and as gifts.

A family of icons, a round stamp and the line “Crafted with Love.” carry the brand onto embroidered patches, engraved needles and hooks, yarn bands, hang tags, gift boxes, shopping bags, project pouches and a webshop, so every piece arrives looking like a gift.

projects.title: DRMC
projects.summary: A fresh, dependable identity that makes a cleaning company look as spotless as the spaces it cleans.
projects.overview: Brand identity for DRMC, a cleaning services company: a duster-and-sun mark and a crisp navy-and-lime palette that say fresh, reliable and professional before the crew even rings the bell.
projects.challenge: Cleaning is a trust business. Clients hand over the keys to their homes and offices, often to people they have never met. DRMC needed to look established and dependable while still feeling fresh and approachable, and to stand apart from the clip-art mops and soap bubbles that crowd the category.
projects.solution: A stacked DRMC monogram in clean geometric capitals carries the authority. A lime duster sweeping past a small sun brings the freshness: the bright, just-cleaned moment built right into the logo. Deep navy says professional, lime says clean, and the pair stays sharp everywhere the brand has to work. It is embroidered on caps and polos so the team is recognised at the door, set on two-sided business cards, and carried onto invoices, where a faint duster watermark turns even the paperwork into a brand touchpoint. The result is a company that looks as organised and spotless as the spaces it leaves behind.

projects.title: UTP
projects.summary: A folded, multicolour identity and campus wayfinding system for a public university in Pereira, Colombia.
projects.overview: Identity, stationery and campus wayfinding for the Universidad Tecnológica de Pereira: a folded, multicolour UTP monogram and a geometric system that make a large public university feel open, modern and easy to navigate.
projects.challenge: A university speaks to everyone at once: prospective students, researchers, staff, visitors and the wider region. UTP needed an identity with the authority of a major institution and the energy of a technology school, one that scales from a business card to a building facade, and a campus that thousands of people can find their way around without having to ask for directions.
projects.solution: The UTP monogram is built like folded paper: ribbons of lime, green, blue, red and orange turn the three letters into one continuous form, technical, energetic and unmistakable at any size. Those same folds break out into a system of origami-like triangles that frame business cards and letterheads, so every piece of correspondence carries the identity without crowding the message. On campus the system becomes wayfinding: tall bilingual directory totems with oversized building numbers, colour-coded floor tags and clear listings let students and visitors find any office, lab or classroom at a glance. From the stone sign at the entrance to the rector's letterhead, the whole university looks and feels like one place.

projects.title: El Rey en su Reino
projects.client: El Rey en su Reino — Book
projects.summary: A warm, hopeful cover and interior for a Spanish-language Bible study.
projects.overview: Cover and interior design for “El Rey en su Reino: Herederos del Reino” by Charles Price, a Spanish-language Bible study: an inviting, uplifting book that feels like a gift before it's opened.
projects.challenge: Study books can look dense and intimidating on the shelf. This one needed a cover that communicates its message of generosity and inheritance at a glance, and an interior that keeps long chapters easy to read.
projects.solution: The cover centres on one image: open hands passing a red gift box, on a soft, light background under an elegant serif title, so the book's message lands before a page is turned. Inside, generous margins, clear chapter openers and a classic serif text face keep the parables and scripture references comfortable to read over long sessions.
